core_intuitions: Mid-training is ONE continuous WSD decay leg, resumed from a PRE-decay stable checkpoint (LR still at peak): the learning rate falls smoothly from peak to floor while the data mix and sequence length change underneath it, across three sub-phases (broad-anneal @2048 -> long-context @8192 -> narrow capability @8192). You do NOT reset the schedule at each boundary or you carve three decay cliffs instead of one clean anneal.

The decay phase is disproportionately valuable: at the end of the constant-LR stable phase the model looks unconverged, then loss bends steeply DOWN the moment decay begins (the WSD 'elbow'). Because the last few percent of tokens commit the representations, feeding PREMIUM data precisely into that decay window (and into its long low-LR tail) is the single highest-leverage data decision in the whole pipeline.

RoPE extrapolation breaks at long positions because the slow (low-frequency) rotation pairs barely turned within the 2048 pretrain window; at position 8192 they swing into angular ranges the model has NEVER seen and attention goes pathological. Raising the RoPE base (theta' = theta * s^(d/(d-2))) slows the whole frequency ladder so positions up to 8192 land back in the learned angular range -- phase-matching (8192*theta'_slow ~ 2048*theta_slow) -- while the FASTEST pair is left essentially untouched, preserving local resolution. NoPE layers have no rotation and need no fix.

The 1-sqrt decay shape drops the LR aggressively early (half of it gone by the 25% mark) where the model still has plasticity to re-organize, then spends a long patient tail near the floor CONSOLIDATING on premium tokens -- which is exactly why capability injection is scheduled LAST, into that low-LR tail.

Going 2048 -> 8192 is 4x longer but makes the attention score matrix 16x larger (quadratic): you must shrink the micro-batch ~4x and hold the ~0.5M-token global batch with gradient accumulation, leaning on GQA + FlashAttention, or you OOM.

A falling scalar perplexity can HIDE a broken long-context tail: validate with loss-versus-position (per-token loss binned by position should keep DECREASING deep into the 8192 window, not rise past 2048) and a needle-in-a-haystack probe -- recovering the needle only in the first 2048 tokens means you have geometry without capability.

new_figures.name: midtrain-continuous-decay-spine
new_figures.concept: The whole chapter on one timeline: a single continuous WSD LR decay from peak to floor across three sub-phases (anneal @2048 -> long-context @8192 -> capability @8192), with the data mixture shifting and the sequence length jumping underneath, and the held-out loss showing the WSD 'elbow' bending steeply down as decay begins.
new_figures.rationale: This is the spine of the chapter and its single most load-bearing intuition: mid-training is ONE decay, not three, with data + seq_len changing under a smoothly falling LR ('broad -> long -> narrow, riding one decreasing learning rate down'). The prose repeatedly warns against resetting the schedule and creating 'decay cliffs', and separately explains why the decay window is where premium data commits (the elbow). A single aligned timeline makes all of that -- the continuity of the LR, the phase budgets, the mix morph, the seq_len jump, and the loss elbow -- readable at a glance and turns three pages of orchestration into one mental picture.

new_figures.name: rope-base-rescale-frequency-ladder
new_figures.concept: Why long-context RoPE breaks and how base rescaling fixes it: the fast (high-frequency) pairs complete many rotations even in 2048 while the slow (low-frequency) pairs barely turn; at position 8192 the slow pairs swing into an angular range the model never saw. Raising the RoPE base slows the whole ladder so position 8192 lands back in the learned angular range (phase-matching), while the fastest pair is untouched.
new_figures.rationale: This is the most math-dense, least-intuitive mechanism in the chapter -- the text spends the whole 'extrapolation problem' + 'base rescaling' + worked-example passage on it, with several formulas and a subtle phase-matching argument (8192*theta'_31 ~ 0.27 rad = 2048*theta_31). A picture of the frequency ladder stretching, with the 'seen' vs 'unseen' angular range shaded and the slow pair being pulled back into the seen range, converts three paragraphs of trigonometry into one geometric idea and makes the d/(d-2) 'leave the fast pair alone' correction obvious.
new_figures.placement: ### RoPE base rescaling (NTK-aware) (anchor right after the theta' = theta * s^(d/(d-2)) equation and its paragraph, before the 'Worked example' admonition)
new_figures.brief: A BEFORE / AFTER contrast built around a 'frequency ladder' of RoPE rotation pairs. Depict the ladder as a vertical stack of a few representative pairs (label them k=0 'fastest / local', a middle pair, and k=31 'slowest / long-range'; note '32 pairs for head_dim d=64'). For each pair draw a little rotating-vector-on-a-dial (a unit vector at an angle) at a couple of reference positions. LEFT PANEL 'Pretrain base theta=10000 (trained only up to position 2048)': for each pair show the angle reached at position 2048 -- the fast pair k=0 has spun through MANY full turns (draw it as a busy dial / 'many rotations'), the slow pair k=31 has barely moved (a tiny wedge, e.g. ~0.27 rad, label 'slow pair barely turns in 2048'). Shade the swept angular range each pair actually SAW during pretraining as a 'SEEN' arc (theme-safe green-ish/positive tint). Then overlay, in a warning tint ('UNSEEN' arc, red-ish/negative), where the SAME original-base pairs would swing if you naively run position 8192: the slow pair k=31 swings 4x further into an arc the model NEVER saw -> caption 'naive 8192: slow dims enter unseen angles -> attention goes pathological'. RIGHT PANEL 'Rescaled base theta ~ 42000 (s=4, exponent d/(d-2)=64/62~1.03)': show the ladder STRETCHED -- every theta_k is smaller so each dial turns MORE SLOWLY; the slow pair k=31 at position 8192 now lands back inside the SEEN arc. Draw the key phase-matching callout as an equality between two dials: 'position 8192 with theta ~ 0.27 rad  ==  position 2048 with theta=10000 ~ 0.27 rad' (same wedge angle) -> label 'positions up to 8192 now fall in the range learned for up to 2048'. Crucially, show the FASTEST pair k=0 as VISUALLY IDENTICAL between left and right panels, labeled 'k=0 unchanged by any base -> local resolution preserved (that is what the d/(d-2) exponent buys)'. Add a small side note box: 'NoPE layers (every 4th) have NO rotation -> untouched by rescaling; call extend_context() ONCE at the sub-phase B boundary, do not re-derive from 10000 again.' Use only the small illustrative integers already in the text (d=64, 2048, 8192, s=4, ~0.27 rad, base 10000 -> ~42000); no other invented numbers. Theme-safe fills, all dials/labels inside the viewBox, clear left-to-right reading order.

new_figures.name: long-context-loss-vs-position-validation
new_figures.concept: Validating that context extension actually took: a falling AVERAGE loss can hide a broken tail, so bin per-token loss by its position within the 8192 window -- a healthy extension keeps decreasing (uses more context to predict better), a broken one rises past ~2048. Plus the needle-in-a-haystack probe: recovering a planted fact only in the first 2048 tokens = geometry without capability.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter makes an explicit, counter-intuitive point that the scalar perplexity metric LIES about long context, and prescribes exactly two cheap during-training probes. Practitioners routinely trust the average and ship a model that cannot attend past its pretrain length. A figure that puts the 'healthy vs broken' loss-versus-position curves side by side, and shows the needle recovered vs lost by depth, makes the failure mode concrete and gives the reader the shape to look for on their own dashboard.
new_figures.placement: ### Validating that the long-context actually works (anchor after the paragraph ending '...train sub-phase B longer or on longer documents.', before the 'Practitioner tip' admonition)
new_figures.brief: Two stacked panels. TOP panel 'Loss vs. position in the 8192 window' -- x-axis = token position within the sequence (0 to 8192; mark the pretrain boundary at 2048 with a dashed vertical line labeled 'pretrain length 2048'), y-axis = average per-token loss (lower = better). Plot TWO curves: (1) HEALTHY (positive/green tint, solid) -- starts a bit higher at the earliest positions and keeps gently DECREASING or flattening as position grows, label 'healthy: model uses MORE context to predict better'; (2) BROKEN (warning/red tint, dashed) -- tracks the healthy curve up to ~2048 then RISES past the pretrain boundary, climbing toward the far positions, label 'broken: far positions are still noise -> rescale+training has not taken'. Add a caption tying to the trap: 'the SCALAR average of either curve can look fine -- only the shape past 2048 reveals the truth'. BOTTOM panel 'Needle-in-a-haystack probe' -- draw a long horizontal bar representing an 8192-token filler document with a small marker ('needle: "the passcode is 4713"') plantable at different depths; show two cases: needle at depth < 2048 -> a check / 'recovered' when prompted 'the passcode is', and needle at depth > 2048 (deep) -> a cross / 'lost -> geometry without capability, train B longer / on longer docs'. Keep it schematic and illustrative (use the text's own example passcode 4713, positions 2048/8192 only); no invented loss numbers -- axes are qualitative/relative. Theme-safe, legible in both themes, all labels inside the viewBox, clear top-to-bottom reading order.

new_figures.name: seqlen-quadratic-attention-budget
new_figures.concept: The quadratic cost of going 2048 -> 8192: 4x longer sequence makes the attention score matrix 16x larger in area/compute, so to fit on one A100 you shrink the micro-batch ~4x and make up the fixed ~0.5M-token global batch with gradient accumulation, while GQA (2 KV heads) and FlashAttention keep memory in check.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter's warning box hinges on a number that trips people up: the jump is 4x in length but 16x in the attention matrix, and the whole 'shrink micro-batch, hold global batch, lean on GQA+Flash' mitigation follows from that. A compact visual of the two score matrices (area = cost) next to the micro-batch/grad-accum rebalance makes the 16x visceral and the fix mechanical, so a reader 'does the arithmetic before launch, not after the OOM' as the text urges.
new_figures.placement: !!! warning "Common pitfall: forgetting the KV-cache and memory blow-up at 8192" (anchor immediately after this warning admonition, at the end of the '## Move 2' section before '### Validating that the long-context actually works')
new_figures.brief: A compact two-part infographic. LEFT 'the quadratic': two square attention score matrices drawn to scale by AREA -- a small square labeled '2048 x 2048' next to a square with 4x the side and therefore ~16x the AREA labeled '8192 x 8192', with a big callout 'sequence 4x longer -> score matrix 16x larger (quadratic), NOT 4x'. Under it note 'FlashAttention never materializes this full matrix; GQA with 2 KV heads shrinks the KV cache 4x -- a big part of why 8192 fits at all.' Row 2 (at 8192): ~4x FEWER sequences per micro-batch (micro_bs ~8) x MORE gradient-accumulation steps -> same 'global batch ~0.5M tokens'. Draw an arrow between the rows labeled 'shrink micro-batch ~4x, raise grad-accum -> global batch (and the LR/batch relationship) unchanged'. summary: A concept-rich chapter with ZERO figures, so the audit is empty and the work is proposing the foundational few. Four static figures are specified, ranked to the intuitions the prose leans on hardest. P1 'midtrain-continuous-decay-spine' is the chapter's spine: a single aligned timeline (LR track + held-out-loss elbow + seq_len step + shifting data-mix bars) that makes the central claim -- mid-training is ONE continuous WSD decay from a pre-decay checkpoint, with data and sequence length changing underneath, 'broad -> long -> narrow, riding one decreasing LR down', no schedule resets/cliffs -- readable at a glance, while also carrying the 'decay window is where premium data commits' (elbow) and 1-sqrt-shape intuitions. P1 'rope-base-rescale-frequency-ladder' tackles the most math-dense mechanism: a before/after frequency-ladder showing slow pairs swinging into UNSEEN angles at 8192, then the raised base slowing the ladder so 8192 phase-matches the learned 2048 range, with the fastest pair provably unchanged (the d/(d-2) point) and NoPE layers untouched. P2 'long-context-loss-vs-position-validation' visualizes the counter-intuitive point that a falling scalar perplexity hides a broken tail -- healthy vs broken loss-vs-position curves plus a needle-depth probe. P3 'seqlen-quadratic-attention-budget' makes the 4x-length-but-16x-attention jump visceral and shows the micro-batch-shrink / grad-accum rebalance that holds the global batch. All theme-safe, illustrative integers only, no invented benchmarks; disciplined coverage of the six core intuitions with no decorative figures.
